# windows

Usage, with examples: [Windows](../reference/windows/README.md). Every resource helper returns a handle that another resource's `dependsOn` accepts.

## windows.npm

npm settings for the current user.

### windows.npm.registries()

Set npm's default registry and `@scope` registries in the user's .npmrc,
leaving authentication, comments and other settings as they are.

```ts
windows.npm.registries(policy: WinNpmRegistryPolicy): Fragment
```

**`policy`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `registries` | `Record<string, { uri: string; }>` | Named registries: HTTPS URLs without credentials, queries or fragments. |
| `default` | `string` | The registry npm uses by default (`registry` in .npmrc). |
| `scopes?` | `Record<string, string>` | npm scope (including |

Returns a fragment: declared when called through a feature's or host's namespace, otherwise return it.

## windows.fonts()

Install fonts for the current user: local .ttf/.otf files, HTTPS
downloads and ZIPs, or Nerd Fonts releases. Downloads are pinned and
checked; find Nerd Fonts names with `winix windows fonts`.

```ts
windows.fonts(spec: { sources: WinFontSource[]; dependsOn?: ResourceHandle | ResourceHandle[]; }): ResourceHandle
```

**`spec`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sources` | `WinFontSource[]` | Paths relative to winix.config.ts, `{ url, files?, sha256? }`, or `{ provider: "nerd-fonts", family, version? }`. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.wallpaper()

Set the desktop background (one image for every display).

```ts
windows.wallpaper(spec: WinWallpaper & { dependsOn?: ResourceHandle | ResourceHandle[]; }): ResourceHandle
```

## windows.settings()

Unified Windows OS settings: call `windows.settings({ ... })` for several
sections at once, or call a section helper directly (`windows.settings.theme()`,
`windows.settings.explorer()`, `windows.settings.developer()`, etc.).

```ts
windows.settings(settings: WinSettings, opts?: WinSettingOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`settings`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `theme?` | `WinThemeSettings` | Theme, color mode, accent color, and transparency. |
| `explorer?` | `WinExplorerSettings` | File Explorer options and sign-in startup delay. |
| `taskbar?` | `WinTaskbarSettings` | Taskbar layout, visibility, search, and multi-monitor options. |
| `start?` | `WinStartSettings` | Start menu folders and lists. |
| `developer?` | `WinDeveloperSettings` | Developer Mode, Sudo for Windows, and Win32 long paths. |
| `clipboard?` | `WinClipboardSettings` | Clipboard History (`Win+V`). |
| `time?` | `WinTimeSettings` | Windows time zone and automatic time zone detection. |
| `keyboard?` | `WinKeyboardSettings` | Keyboard repeat delay and repeat speed. |
| `mouse?` | `WinMouseSettings` | Mouse pointer speed, pointer precision, and button swap. |
| `notifications?` | `WinNotificationSettings` | USB and weak-charger system notifications. |

**`theme`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `colorMode?` | `WinColorMode \| { apps?: WinColorMode; system?: WinColorMode; }` | Light or dark mode. One value sets apps and system alike; the object form sets them separately. Applied per-user without elevation. |
| `accentColor?` | `string` | Accent color as `"#RRGGBB"`; turns off automatic accent coloring. Applied per-user. |
| `autoColorization?` | `boolean` | Pick the accent color from the wallpaper automatically. Applied elevated. |
| `transparency?` | `boolean` | Enable window transparency effects. Applied elevated. |
| `accentOnStartAndTaskbar?` | `boolean` | Show the accent color on Start and the taskbar. Applied elevated. |
| `accentOnTitleBars?` | `boolean` | Show the accent color on title bars and window borders. Applied elevated. |

**`explorer`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `showExtensions?` | `boolean` | Show file name extensions. |
| `showHiddenFiles?` | `boolean` | Show hidden files (protected operating-system files stay hidden). |
| `openTo?` | `WinExplorerOpenTo` | The folder a new File Explorer window opens to. |
| `showFullPathInTitleBar?` | `boolean` | Show the full folder path in File Explorer's title bar. |
| `classicContextMenu?` | `boolean` | Use the classic Windows 10 right-click context menu on Windows 11. |
| `compactMode?` | `boolean` | Use compact spacing in File Explorer lists. |
| `startupDelay?` | `boolean` | `false` removes Explorer's sign-in delay before starting Run entries and Startup shortcuts. |
| `waitForIdle?` | `boolean` | `false` stops Explorer waiting for an idle desktop at sign-in before starting startup entries. |

**`taskbar`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alignment?` | `WinTaskbarAlignment` | Taskbar icons on the left or centered. Applied elevated. |
| `autoHide?` | `boolean` | Hide the taskbar until the pointer reaches it. Applied live per-user. |
| `search?` | `WinTaskbarSearchMode` | How search appears on the taskbar. Applied per-user. |
| `taskView?` | `boolean` | Show the Task View button. Applied per-user. |
| `widgets?` | `boolean` | Show the Widgets button. Applied per-user. |
| `endTask?` | `boolean` | Show "End task" in the taskbar right-click menu. Applied per-user. |
| `badges?` | `boolean` | Show unread badges on taskbar icons. Applied elevated. |
| `grouping?` | `WinTaskbarGroupingMode` | When taskbar buttons of one app combine. Applied elevated. |
| `multiMonitor?` | `boolean` | Show the taskbar on every display. Applied elevated. |
| `multiMonitorMode?` | `WinTaskbarMultiMonMode` | Which taskbar shows a window's button across multiple monitors. Applied elevated. |

**`start`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `folders?` | `WinStartFolder[]` | Folders shown next to Start's power button. |
| `showRecent?` | `boolean` | Show recently opened items in Start. |
| `showRecommended?` | `boolean` | Show recommendations in Start. |

**`developer`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode?` | `boolean` | Developer Mode, which allows symlinks without elevation (`windows.file.symlink()` auto-depends on `mode: true`). |
| `sudo?` | `WinSudoMode` | Sudo for Windows mode (`"disabled"`, `"newWindow"`, `"disableInput"`, or `"inline"`). |
| `longPaths?` | `boolean` | Enable Win32 long paths (paths over 260 characters). |

**`clipboard`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `history?` | `boolean` | Enable Clipboard History (`Win+V`). |

**`time`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zone?` | `string` | Windows time zone ID (for example `"Pacific Standard Time"` or `"W. Europe Standard Time"`). |
| `automaticZone?` | `boolean` | Set the time zone automatically from location. |

**`keyboard`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## windows.registry

Manage Windows registry keys and values declaratively through the native
`Microsoft.Windows/Registry` DSC resource. Machine hives elevate automatically.

```ts
windows.registry.set("HKCU\\Software\\MyApp", "Theme", "dark");
windows.registry.set("HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\MyApp", "Enabled", 1);
windows.registry.remove("HKCU\\Software\\MyApp", "OldFlag");
```

### windows.registry.set()

Set a Windows registry value through the native `Microsoft.Windows/Registry`
DSC resource. Pass `""` as `valueName` to set the key's `(Default)` value.
Machine hives (`HKLM`, `HKCR`, `HKU`, `HKCC`) run in switch's elevated step automatically.

```ts
windows.registry.set(keyPath: string, valueName: string, value: WinRegistryValue, opts?: WinRegistrySetOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type?` | `WinRegistryValueType` | Registry value kind. Inferred when omitted: strings become `"string"`, numbers become `"dword"`, string arrays become `"multiString"`, and number arrays become `"binary"`. Specify `"expandString"` or `"qword"` explicitly. |
| `elevated?` | `boolean` | Run in switch's elevated step. Defaults to true for machine hives (`HKLM`, `HKCR`, `HKU`, `HKCC`) and false for `HKCU`. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.registry.remove()

Ensure a Windows registry key does not exist, through `Microsoft.Windows/Registry`.
Machine hives (`HKLM`, `HKCR`, `HKU`, `HKCC`) run in switch's elevated step automatically.
Ensure a Windows registry value (pass `""` for the `(Default)` value) does
not exist, through `Microsoft.Windows/Registry`.

```ts
windows.registry.remove(keyPath: string, opts?: WinRegistryRemoveOpts): ResourceHandle
windows.registry.remove(keyPath: string, valueName: string, opts?: WinRegistryRemoveOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `elevated?` | `boolean` | Run in switch's elevated step. Defaults to true for machine hives (`HKLM`, `HKCR`, `HKU`, `HKCC`) and false for `HKCU`. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.wsl()

WSL itself (`windows.wsl()`) and its distros (`windows.wsl.distro()`).

```ts
windows.wsl(opts?: WinWslOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config?` | `WinWslConfig` | Manage the whole ~/.wslconfig (left alone when omitted). Applies when WSL restarts. |
| `force?` | `boolean` | Replace a differing target without a backup (`backup: true` still backs up). Never deletes a directory with files. |
| `backup?` | `boolean` | Default true: move a differing existing target to `<target>.bak` first. false: fail instead of replacing it. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

**`config`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wsl2?` | `{ memory?: string; processors?: number; swap?: string; localhostForwarding?: boolean; networkingMode?: "nat" \| "mirrored" \| "none" \| "virtioproxy"; dnsTunneling?: boolean; firewall?: boolean; autoProxy?: boolean; guiApplications?: boolean; }` | The `[wsl2]` section of .wslconfig. |
| `experimental?` | `{ autoMemoryReclaim?: "disabled" \| "gradual" \| "dropCache"; sparseVhd?: boolean; }` | The `[experimental]` section of .wslconfig. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.wsl.distro()

Create an absent distro or adopt a matching WSL 2/NixOS/Linux hostname registration.

```ts
windows.wsl.distro(name: string, spec: WinWslDistroSpec): ResourceHandle
```

**`spec`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default?` | `boolean` | Make it the default distro (`wsl` without `-d`). At most one per host; only for distros Winix creates. |
| `host?` | `string \| HostDef` | Expected Linux hostname for adoption (a name or `host(...)` value); defaults to setup.host. |
| `setup?` | `WinWslSetupSpec` | First-run setup for Winix-created distros; never run for adopted distros. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Extra resources to apply first; WSL itself, its features and .wslconfig are added automatically. |
| `source` | `"nixos-wsl"` | The image: "nixos-wsl", the official NixOS-WSL release (pinned in winix-windows.lock). |
| `installLocation` | `WinFilePath` | Creation destination; an adopted distro keeps its registered location. |

**`setup`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | `string` | HTTPS Git URL, or "self": use the tracked remote of the checkout holding winix.config.ts (SSH remotes are converted to HTTPS). With "self", `ref` defaults to the current upstream branch (or commit when detached) and `configDirectory` to the config's path within the repository. |
| `configDirectory?` | `string` | Required unless `repository` is "self". |
| `host` | `string \| HostDef` | Linux host to activate: its name, or the value returned by `host(...)`. |
| `user?` | `string \| AccountUserRef` | Linux account: its name, or the factory returned by `account.user(...)`. |
| `ref?` | `string` | Branch, tag, full ref, or immutable commit; resolved into winix-windows.lock. Defaults to HEAD. |
| `checkout?` | `string` | Absolute path inside the selected account's home. Defaults to <home>/dotfiles. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.startup

Programs started at sign-in (logon tasks or Startup shortcuts), never run during apply.

### windows.startup.app()

Start a program when the current user signs in, through a per-user logon
task in Task Scheduler's \Winix\ folder: it starts right after sign-in,
not after every other startup entry like the Startup folder. Never run
during apply; no elevation needed.

```ts
windows.startup.app(name: string, spec: WinStartupAppSpec): ResourceHandle
```

**`spec`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `windowStyle?` | `WinStartupAppWindowStyle` | "hidden" runs console programs without a window. Defaults to "normal". |
| `delay?` | `number` | Seconds after sign-in before it starts (0 to 3600). Defaults to 0. |
| `executable` | `ResourceHandle \| WinFilePath` | Path, application name, or a windows.file.* handle (its target is used and the file becomes a dependency). The same applies to arguments and workingDirectory. |
| `arguments?` | `(ResourceHandle \| WinFilePath)[]` | Arguments, passed as they are (standard Windows quoting). Known folders and file handles become their paths. |
| `workingDirectory?` | `ResourceHandle \| WinFilePath` | The folder it starts in. Defaults to the user profile; must exist when the switch runs. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first, such as the program's package. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.startup.shortcut()

A shortcut in the current user's Startup folder, which Explorer opens last at sign-in.

```ts
windows.startup.shortcut(name: string, spec: WinStartupShortcutSpec): ResourceHandle
```

**`spec`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `windowStyle?` | `WinStartupWindowStyle` | "normal" (default), "minimized" or "maximized". |
| `backup?` | `boolean` | Move a different existing shortcut of this name to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Winix\startup-backups (default unless force). |
| `force?` | `boolean` | Replace a different existing shortcut without a backup. |
| `executable` | `ResourceHandle \| WinFilePath` | Path, application name, or a windows.file.* handle (its target is used and the file becomes a dependency). The same applies to arguments and workingDirectory. |
| `arguments?` | `(ResourceHandle \| WinFilePath)[]` | Arguments, passed as they are (standard Windows quoting). Known folders and file handles become their paths. |
| `workingDirectory?` | `ResourceHandle \| WinFilePath` | The folder it starts in. Defaults to the user profile; must exist when the switch runs. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first, such as the program's package. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.


| Option | Type | Description |

### windows.powershell.profile()

Link (or copy) the current user's PowerShell profile from `source`.
The target is `$PROFILE.CurrentUserCurrentHost`, i.e. Documents (OneDrive
redirection included) \\PowerShell (or WindowsPowerShell for 5.1).

```ts
windows.powershell.profile(source: string | URL, opts?: WinPowerShellProfileOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shell?` | `"pwsh" \| "windowspowershell"` | "pwsh" (PowerShell 7, default) or "windowspowershell" (Windows PowerShell 5.1). |
| `mode?` | `"symlink" \| "copy"` | "symlink" (default) keeps the file live-linked to the checkout; "copy" writes a copy. |
| `force?` | `boolean` | Replace a differing target without a backup (`backup: true` still backs up). Never deletes a directory with files. |
| `backup?` | `boolean` | Default true: move a differing existing target to `<target>.bak` first. false: fail instead of replacing it. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.configPath()

Absolute path of `path` relative to the directory holding winix.config.ts,
resolved when the workspace is evaluated, e.g. `windows.configPath("..")`
for the repository root. For values such as environment variables;
file sources are already config-relative.

```ts
windows.configPath(path?: string): string
```

## windows.package()

Declare a winget/msstore package.

```ts
windows.package("Git.Git")
windows.package({ source: "msstore", id: "9NKSQGP7F2NH" })
windows.package({ id: "Git.Git", version: "2.44.0" })
windows.package("Valve.Steam", { version: "any" }) // self-updating: any version
```

```ts
windows.package(arg: WinPackageArg, opts?: WinPackageOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`arg`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | WinGet id (`Git.Git`, case-insensitive) or Microsoft Store product id. Find ids with `winix windows search`. |
| `source?` | `WinPackageSource` | "winget" (default) or "msstore". |
| `version?` | `string` | Omitted: pinned in winix-windows.lock (newer installs are kept). `"1.2.3"`: exactly this version. `"any"`: installed in any version; for apps that update themselves or report no usable version. Never locked, compared or downgraded. |
| `elevated?` | `boolean` | The installers need administrator rights though WinGet can't tell: install in switch's elevated step. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources this package must be applied after. Accepts a single handle or an array of handles returned by resource-producing `windows.*` helpers. |

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source?` | `WinPackageSource` | "winget" (default) or "msstore". |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources this package must be applied after. Accepts a single handle or an array of handles returned by resource-producing `windows.*` helpers. |
| `version?` | `string` | Omitted: pinned in winix-windows.lock (newer installs are kept). `"1.2.3"`: exactly this version. `"any"`: installed in any version; for apps that update themselves or report no usable version. Never locked, compared or downgraded. |
| `elevated?` | `boolean` | The installers need administrator rights though WinGet can't tell: install in switch's elevated step. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.raw()

Run an arbitrary command on every Windows switch as a
command resource.

This is an escape hatch, not a declarative/idempotent helper: a raw
command has no test phase, so it runs on every `winix switch`. Prefer
typed helpers when available.
Command strings run in PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`); explicit executables are preserved.

```ts
windows.raw("New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:USERPROFILE\\.local\\bin")
windows.raw({ executable: "pwsh", arguments: ["-Command", "Write-Host hi"] })
windows.raw({ name: "make-bin-dir", executable: "cmd", arguments: ["/c", "mkdir", "foo"] })
```

```ts
windows.raw(arg: WinRawCommandArg): ResourceHandle
```

**`arg`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name?` | `string` | A stable name for the resource (in the plan and in dependsOn ordering). Defaults to one derived from the command. |
| `executable` | `string` | The program to run: a path or a name on PATH. |
| `arguments?` | `string[]` | Its arguments, passed as they are (no shell). |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources this command must run after. Accepts a single handle or an array of handles. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.dsc()

Declare an arbitrary DSC v3 resource (escape hatch). The `type` is a fully
qualified DSC resource type and `properties` is serialized verbatim to the
generated configuration. Use this for resources Winix has no typed helper
for.

```ts
windows.dsc({
  type: "Microsoft.Windows/Service",
  properties: { name: "spooler", startType: "automatic" },
});
```

```ts
windows.dsc(arg: WinDscSpec): ResourceHandle
```

**`arg`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | Fully qualified DSC resource type, e.g. "Microsoft.Windows/Service". |
| `name?` | `string` | A stable name for the resource (in the plan and the generated configuration). |
| `properties?` | `WinDscProperties` | The resource's properties, passed to DSC as they are. |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.env

Manage a user/machine environment variable declaratively via the native
`Microsoft.Windows/Registry` DSC resource.

```ts
windows.env.set("EDITOR", "nvim");
windows.env.remove("OLD_VAR");
```

### windows.env.set()

Set an environment variable for the user (default) or the machine. New terminals see it; running programs keep their old environment.

```ts
windows.env.set(name: string, value: string, opts?: WinEnvOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scope?` | `WinEnvScope` | "user" (default) or "machine" (needs administrator rights; joins the elevated step). |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.env.remove()

Make sure an environment variable is not set.

```ts
windows.env.remove(name: string, opts?: WinEnvOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**: the same options as [windows.env.set()](#windowsenvset).

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.path

Ensure a directory is on the PATH, appending/removing surgically via an
idempotent `Microsoft.DSC.Transitional/PowerShellScript` resource.

```ts
windows.path.add("%USERPROFILE%\\.local\\bin");
windows.path.remove("%USERPROFILE%\\.old-bin");
```

### windows.path.add()

Add one entry to PATH, leaving the rest as it is. `%VARIABLE%` entries stay unexpanded.

```ts
windows.path.add(value: string, opts?: WinEnvOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**: the same options as [windows.env.set()](#windowsenvset).

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.path.remove()

Remove one entry from PATH.

```ts
windows.path.remove(value: string, opts?: WinEnvOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**: the same options as [windows.env.set()](#windowsenvset).

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

## windows.file

Manage files, copies, and dotfile symlinks declaratively via an idempotent
`Microsoft.DSC.Transitional/PowerShellScript` resource.

```ts
windows.file.text("%USERPROFILE%\\.gitconfig", "[user]\n");
windows.file.symlink("%LOCALAPPDATA%\\nvim", "%USERPROFILE%\\dotfiles\\nvim");
windows.file.copy("%APPDATA%\\tool\\config.json", ".\\config.json");
windows.file.remove("%USERPROFILE%\\.oldrc");
```

### windows.file.text()

A file with exactly this content.

```ts
windows.file.text(target: WinFilePath, content: string, opts?: WinFileOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `force?` | `boolean` | Replace a differing target without a backup (`backup: true` still backs up). Never deletes a directory with files. |
| `backup?` | `boolean` | Default true: move a differing existing target to `<target>.bak` first. false: fail instead of replacing it. |
| `recursive?` | `boolean` | symlink of a directory: create the tree and link each file, instead of linking the directory itself. |
| `elevate?` | `boolean` | Write in switch's elevated step, for targets the user can't write. |
| `encoding?` | `WinFileEncoding` | text: "utf8" (default), "utf8bom" or "ascii". |
| `dependsOn?` | `ResourceHandle \| ResourceHandle[]` | Resources to apply first. |

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.file.symlink()

A link to `source` (relative to winix.config.ts, or absolute). Live: editing
the file in the checkout changes it on the machine, with no switch. Needs
Developer Mode or elevation.

```ts
windows.file.symlink(target: WinFilePath, source: string | URL, opts?: WinFileOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**: the same options as [windows.file.text()](#windowsfiletext).

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.file.copy()

A copy of `source` (relative to winix.config.ts, or absolute); a copy changed on the machine is replaced by the next switch.

```ts
windows.file.copy(target: WinFilePath, source: string | URL, opts?: WinFileOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**: the same options as [windows.file.text()](#windowsfiletext).

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.

### windows.file.remove()

Make sure `target` doesn't exist.

```ts
windows.file.remove(target: WinFilePath, opts?: WinFileOpts): ResourceHandle
```

**`opts`**: the same options as [windows.file.text()](#windowsfiletext).

Returns a handle, for another resource's `dependsOn`.
